title: Fold executor-reported Windows separators to POSIX canonical artifact names
required_tests: src/__tests__/pair-f1-artifact-authority.test.ts#Windows path forms rejected as invalid syntax
description: BASE 02c5944, R1 (audit corrections). artifact-validation.ts folds executor-reported backslashes to '/' then rejects Windows path syntax on EVERY host via isWindowsPathForm(): drive-qualified 'C:/x' (post-fold 'C:\x'), drive-relative 'C:rel', and folded UNC '//srv/sh' — POSIX path.isAbsolute alone would mint a literal 'C:/x' canonical name on Linux (R1-F1). Rejection happens at the syntax check ('artifact path invalid'), before filesystem resolve; traversal '..', absolute POSIX, allowed_paths, symlink, sha256/byte_size checks unchanged. scripts/dev-verification/lib.mjs R1-F2: pair-f2-r4-remediation tolerated baseline tightened from /.+/ to title-scoped /^(?:A[1-7]|B1)\./ max 8 — matcher sees test titles only; exit-127 unix-spawn cause verified manually (documented limitation); any new failure in that file is FAIL. Tests: A1b backslash→PASS POSIX name, A1c '..\x'→FAIL zero rows, A1d 4 Windows path forms→'artifact path invalid' FAIL zero rows on every OS (failing-first verified: C:rel previously died downstream as 'artifact missing', POSIX would accept C:/x). No architecture change.
